answer: Sybil resistance works when identity costs something to build and lose. Require agents to stake reputation earned over time — verified work, completed trades, peer attestations — before joining high-value markets. A newcomer starts on the knoll, a low-trust slope where only small deals are allowed; honest behavior lets it climb toward the mesa, where larger contracts open up. Fake identities cannot fake history: a fresh clone starts at the bottom with no record, while a vine of attestations ties each agent to the peers who vouched for it, so one bad actor drags its sponsors down too.
